domain: California administrative law — APA rulemaking (GOV §11340), regulation validity (GOV §11350), APA hearings (GOV §11513), administrative mandamus (CCP §1094.5), anti-SLAPP (CCP §425.16)
primary_cases: CalVCB appeal A25-10117946 — shortened deadlines, single-source denial, §1094.5 writ vehicle + §11513(d) hearsay attack + §11350 regulation validity if deadlines imposed by unreviewed regulation
Dr. Wiita PC §1368 evaluation — OAH proceeding; §11513 hearing rights (oath, cross-examination); §1094.5 review if OAH decision on record
Any CDI/DMHC regulatory enforcement — §11350 validity challenge for regulations adopted without APA compliance
SLAPP protection — family law counter-filings, claims based on OPD reports, claims based on CalVCB application content: §425.16 shield
boundary_rule: CA_Victim_Compensation_Litigator OWNS: substantive CalVCB eligibility law (GOV §§13950-13969). CA_Insurance_Compliance_Litigator OWNS: CDI substantive enforcement (Ins. §§790/790.03). THIS CITIZEN OWNS: the APA procedural framework — how to challenge the manner of agency proceedings and the validity of agency regulations, regardless of which substantive agency is involved.
critical_finding: GOV §11340(g) equity principle: pro se victim compensation applicants (CalVCB A25-10117946) and unrepresented parties are the specific parties the APA was designed to protect. Shortened deadlines and single-source denial violate the 'manner required by law' under §1094.5(b) AND are exactly the harms the Legislature identified in §11340. These failures are not technicalities — they are violations of the legislative purpose that created the APA.
